correctness.rationale: A direct induction on word degree reconstructs a simultaneous conjugation for every field. On each source/target Boolean weight component, idempotence forces equal-weight corrections to vanish, and pairwise commutation gives a common potential removable by a single shear. The automorphism order and stabilizer order are independently derived from generator substitutions, yielding the all-arity formula and ranks. A direct original-algebra exhaustive check covers all maps over F2 and F3 in the six-dimensional case, all pairs in both fields and all binary triples; no finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Published primary theorem statements and accessible prior claim records were checked for the same objects, aliases, semilattice reductions and stronger finite-field enumerators. No identical or dominating coverage was found. Berzins and Lipyanski classify automorphisms of an endomorphism semigroup rather than algebra-automorphism conjugacy of families of commuting idempotent elements. Fountain–Gould concerns products of idempotents. A more general formal linearization theorem could subsume the structural claim; an incompletely inspected 1998 retracts paper remains a historical risk. Novelty is asserted only provisionally under those limitations.

value.rationale: The natural semilattice-action problem receives a complete field-independent orbit classification and a finite-field count for every arity, generator number and nilpotence length. Exact joint ranks on the entire algebra and the Boolean-AND nonlinear stabilizer exponent are structural invariants beyond the already-known linear diagonalization. The factor \(q^2\) separating incomparable and comparable support types in the smallest nontrivial example demonstrates that the nonlinear count answers a motivated question rather than a renamed linear formula.
